battle.name: 隋擊契丹之戰
battle.brief: 大業元年四月，契丹寇高麗，高麗遣使乞師，隋煬帝以宇文愷、封德彝為行軍總管，發兵自柳城北進。隋軍深入而糧道不繼，終為契丹游騎所乘，全軍崩潰，士卒死傷以萬計。翌年再發兵，契丹避戰請降，內附於隋。亞述長弓不在此役，但它代表的複合反曲弓技術，正是契丹角弓的源流。

kit.name: 亞述長弓
kit.history: 亞述人靠弓和鐵的組合征服兩河流域。弓兵在車上射，車兵靠弓兵開路。

countries: 大業元年四月，交戰的兩方是隋朝與契丹松漠部；站在契丹身後的並非盟友，而是同樣被隋廷視為北方勁敵的突厥，契丹人自己則是夾在隋、突厥與高麗三面之間。隋軍方面，煬帝以宇文愷、封德彝為行軍總管，發兵自幽州、柳城一線北進，兵源以河北、江南徵發的丁壯與新附軍人為主，步騎兼備而步兵居多，另配弩手與護糧的車、駕牛。指揮系統上，行軍總管之下設行軍長史與軍曹參軍分軍部署，後方以幽州、柳城兩處邊州為屯糧與轉輸之樞，昌黎、盧龍一線供芻粟，糧秣全賴陸運，隨軍在草原上既無城可屯、又無柵可守。契丹方面，部眾居於白狼水（大凌河）以北的松漠草原，以松漠部為主，與庫莫奚、室韋為鄰，部落散處，無城郭，以騎兵為主力，少長皆習弓馬，遊牧為生，遇戰則合、戰罷則分，沒有集中的城防，也沒有固定的國界線。部落之上有首領大業，其下分為若干部帳，各部渠帥分領其眾。此外高麗並未一兵一卒參戰，它的角色是派使到隋廷請援，把隋朝推上戰場；北方草原的整體格局是，隋朝想以契丹受創為楔子，插在突厥與高麗之間，契丹則要在兩強之間保住游牧地的餘地。
countriesEn: In the fourth month of the first year of Daye the two belligerents were the Sui dynasty and the Songmo branch of the Khitan; what stood behind the Khitan was not an ally but the Turks, whom the Sui court likewise regarded as the northern enemy, while the Khitan themselves were wedged between the Sui, the Turks and Koguryŏ on three sides. On the Sui side Emperor Yang appointed Yúwén Kǎi and Fēng Déyí as overall commanders of the expeditionary army and sent it north from the line of Yōuzhōu and Liǔchéng. The troops were drawn mainly from levies conscripted in Hébĕi and Jiāngnán together with newly submitted soldiers, mixed infantry and cavalry with the infantry in the majority, plus crossbowmen and the wagons and draught oxen that guarded the supply train. The command system placed a military registrar and a staff of army registrars under the overall commanders, with the army divided into columns; in the rear the frontier prefectures of Yōuzhōu and Liǔchéng served as the pivot of depots and transshipment, the district of Chānglí and Lúlóng supplying fodder and grain, and every bushel travelled by land, for on the grassland the army had neither a city in which to quarter nor a stockade in which to hold. On the Khitan side the people lived on the Songmo grassland north of the White Wolf River, the modern Dà Líng, the main body being the Songmo tribe, neighbours of the Kumoxi and the Xīwéi. Their settlements were scattered, they had no walled towns, cavalry was their strength, young and old alike were drilled in bow and horse, they lived by herding and moved with the pastures, and in battle they came together and after it dispersed again, having no concentrated defences and no fixed frontier line. Above the tribes stood the chieftain Dà Yè, and under him a number of separate tribal camps, each led by its own khan. Goryeo, meanwhile, contributed not a single soldier: its role was to send an embassy to the Sui court asking for help, which pushed the Sui onto the battlefield. The wider northern picture was this: the Sui wanted a wounded Khitan to serve as a wedge driven between the Turks and Goryeo, while the Khitan sought to preserve the margin of their grazing grounds between two powers.
people: 這場戰爭裡真正做決定的是隋煬帝楊廣。隋文帝在位時，契丹已屢次內侵高麗，隋廷出過兵卻未能把對方羈縻住，邊患一直懸著；煬帝大業元年即位，四月正沿北巡的隊伍駐於柳城一線，接到高麗的請援後即下詔出兵。一名剛登基的皇帝把第一次軍事冒險押在北方草原上，這個決定本身就定了此役的規模與風險。行軍總管宇文愷是營造東都與長城的老匠人，雖有才於土木而素不習軍旅，臨陣調度只能倚賴舊例；同行的封德彝是朝中重臣，長於籌策，兩人搭配在隋廷眼中正是文治與武功的象徵，卻被派去對付最難纏的草原騎兵。另一端的關鍵人物是契丹首領大業：隋朝屍次出兵逼他臣服，他先以游騎周旋、最後才遣使內附，他的選擇決定了此役的收場方式。史籍對具體的營級指揮者著墨極少，雙方前線的渠帥、旗頭姓名多已不可考，這也是《隋書》與《資治通鑑》在本役的戰鬥細節上顯得空疏的原因之一；較可追索的，是此役之後宇文愷仍主持東都與長城工程、封德彝不久病卒於任上，而這位內附的契丹首領在隋亡之後，其部眾又兩度北走與復叛。
peopleEn: The man who really decided this war was Emperor Yang of Sui, Yang Guang. Under Emperor Wen the Khitan had already raided Goryeo repeatedly; the Sui had sent troops against them and had not succeeded in holding them in submission, and the frontier trouble had remained unsettled. In the first year of Daye, in the fourth month, while the emperor was on his northern tour with his column posted in the line of Liǔchéng, the plea for help from Goryeo arrived and he issued the order to march. A ruler newly come to the throne staked his first military gamble on the northern grassland, and that decision alone fixed the scale and the risk of the campaign. The overall commander Yúwén Kǎi was the old master builder of the eastern capital and the great wall, gifted in works of civil engineering but wholly unpractised in the field, so that his handling of the battle could only lean on precedent; his colleague Fēng Déyí was a heavyweight of the court, skilled in planning, and the pair together were meant to represent civil rule and military command at once, yet they were sent against the most elusive cavalry on the steppe. The decisive figure on the other side was the Khitan chieftain Dà Yè. The Sui had campaigned against him repeatedly in order to make him submit; he first parried with his mobile horsemen and only at the end sent an embassy to surrender, and the choice he made that way decided how the war ended. The histories say almost nothing about individual unit commanders, and the names of the Khitan khan and the standard-bearers on both sides have largely been lost, which is one reason why the History of Sui and the Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance are so thin on the fighting details of this campaign. What can be traced is that afterwards Yúwén Kǎi still directed the works on the eastern capital and the wall, that Fēng Déyí died of illness in office shortly after, and that after the Sui collapsed the tribes of the chieftain who had submitted drifted north again and rebelled twice more.
kits: 卡面這件亞述長弓，學名 Assyrian bow，是公元前七世紀亞述人所用的複合反曲弓：角、骨或木為弓臂主體，筋腱製弦，短而有力，張力大、拉距短，最利於騎射與車上射擊；亞述人靠弓與鐵的組合征兩河流域，弓兵在車上射，車兵靠弓兵開路。這件兵器並不在大業元年的柳城原野上，亞述早已滅亡，東亞的弓兵用的是弓、弩與鎗，兩者並無直接的裝備傳承。技術同源之處在於材料哲學：亞述以牛角配筋，草原的契丹與突厥同樣以羊角、牛角為弓臂、筋腱為弦，角弓是北方遊牧騎兵的基本裝備，也是契丹人自幼操練的技藝。真正上陣的隋軍裝備以弩為主、弓為輔，蹶張弩與步弩用於野戰射擊，鎗、槊、刀、盾與鐵甲披膊配給步兵，騎兵用馬槊與環首刀；契丹一方以角弓、箭、皮甲與木盾為主，長矛與蒙皮鈍器輔之，而他們真正的重裝備是馬匹。運輸方面，隋軍靠車與駕牛運糧，糧道一斷全軍即瓦解；亞述弓兵所倚靠的車陣，在隋軍這裡只剩下運糧的功能，形同虛設。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Assyrian bow, a composite recurve used by the Assyrians in the seventh century BC: horn, bone or wood forms the body of the bow limb, sinew is spun into the string, and the weapon is short and powerful, with high tension and short draw, which makes it ideal for mounted archery and for shooting from a chariot. The Assyrians conquered the two river plains with the combination of bow and iron, the archers shooting from the wagons and the chariot corps riding behind the archers' fire. This weapon was not on the fields of Liǔchéng in the first year of Daye: Assyria had been destroyed long since, and the archers of East Asia used bows, crossbows and halberds, with no direct line of equipment between the two. The technical kinship lies in the logic of materials. The Assyrians matched horn with sinew, and the Khitan and Turks of the steppe did exactly the same, using sheep horn and ox horn for the limbs and sinew for the string; the composite horn bow was the basic kit of the nomadic horseman and the craft the Khitan drilled from childhood. The Sui order of battle that actually fought relied on the crossbow first and the bow second, with the two-man drawn crossbow and the hand crossbow used for field shooting, halberds, spears, sabres, shields and iron armour given to the infantry, and cavalry armed with horse lances and ring-pommel sabres. The Khitan side fought with composite bows, arrows, leather armour and wooden shields, with long spears and hide-covered blunt weapons to support them, and their real heavy equipment was the horse. On the logistics side the Sui carried grain in wagons drawn by oxen, and once the supply line was cut the whole army came apart; the chariot formation on which the Assyrian archers depended had been reduced in the Sui army to a baggage train, decorative rather than functional.
tactics: 隋軍的打法是典型的中原遠征模式：大軍直線推進，車隊夾在隊列之間，步軍在前結陣，騎兵與弩手列於兩翼及後隊，遇敵即列陣而戰。問題出在節奏上。柳城距契丹松漠數百里，其間多為草原與沙碩地，隋軍無城可屯、無柵可守，只能一面向前搜索一面維持糧道；行軍縱隊越拉越長，護衛一旦被游騎切斷，糧車便成為獵物。契丹的戰法正好相反：不與隋軍正面列陣，遊騎不斷貼近射擾，迫其分兵、迫其收攏陣形，等隋軍的士氣與體力被拖到極處，再集中精騎攻其一翼。隋軍的崩潰正出現在這種消耗之後，縱隊被切、糧隊被襲，前軍回援時隊形自相踐踏，全軍因而被衝垮，而隋朝自從未把契丹主力一次誘入預設陣地。翌年再戰，契丹不再接受野戰，遣使請降，隋軍得以不戰而羈縻其眾。亞述式的戰法本是另一條路，以箭雨覆蓋敵陣、以車兵趁隙衝鋒，弓與車配合完成整場戰鬥；這套組合在開闊草原上並不適用，契丹人用馬匹替代了車，用角弓替代了亞述弓，但那個以射手決定節奏的核心並沒有改變。
tacticsEn: The Sui method was the classic Chinese style of distant expedition: the main body marched in a straight line, the baggage wagons ran between the columns, the infantry formed up in front, the cavalry and the crossbowmen were placed on the flanks and in the rear, and when the enemy appeared the army deployed and fought. The trouble lay in the tempo. Liǔchéng lay several hundred li from the Songmo grassland of the Khitan, and the country between was steppe and sand flats. The Sui had no city in which to quarter and no stockade in which to hold; they could only press forward in search of the enemy while keeping the grain line alive, and the marching column grew longer as it went. The moment the escort was cut by the mobile horsemen the grain wagons became the prey. The Khitan method was the exact opposite: they never offered a set battle, their outriders rode up and shot continuously, forcing the Sui to spread out and to close up, and when the Sui troops' morale and strength had been ground down to the limit they concentrated their best horse on one wing. The collapse of the Sui army came after exactly this kind of exhaustion, with the column cut and the baggage attacked, the advance troops wheeling back to help and trampling each other, and the whole army breaking under the charge. The Sui never once managed to lure the main body of the Khitan into a prepared position. In the second year the Khitan no longer accepted a pitched battle and sent an embassy to surrender, so the Sui could take them into submission without fighting. The Assyrian method was a different road entirely: a rain of arrows to cover the enemy host, chariot troops charging in the gaps, bow and chariot working together to carry the whole engagement. That combination does not work on open grassland. The Khitan replaced the chariot with the horse and the Assyrian bow with a composite horn bow, but the core of the matter, the bowman setting the tempo of the fight, did not change.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。時間：隋文帝開皇末年契丹已寇高麗，隋廷曾出兵而未竟；大業元年四月，隋煬帝下詔發兵，兵敗；大業二年再發兵，契丹請降內附，隋廷於其地置州安置；隋末契丹復叛，唐貞觀十八年再內附於唐。兵力：史書記隋軍出師號稱三十萬，這是《資治通鑑》所載的出征總數，實際能投入戰鬥與護糧的比例遠低於此；契丹兵力史無明文，只知其以遊騎作戰，兵眾分散於各部帳，說其精騎以數萬計者並無可靠記載可以坐實。損失：第一次戰敗，隋軍多敗績，士卒死亡以萬計，軍資器械盡委之於敵，《隋書》與《資治通鑑》都只作死者甚眾的概括，並無更細的數目。距離：柳城郡（今遼寧朝陽）距東都洛陽約一千五百里上下，柳城至契丹松漠又數百里，糧秣全靠牛車陸運，一往一返逾兩千里，中間沒有可以屯糧的城池。制度數字：隋朝於契丹內附後置州縣以處其眾，內附人數史無記載，僅可推知為部眾的一部分而非整個部族；大業二年時，隋廷仍以啟民可汗為北方盟友，自北面牽制契丹，契丹正是在南北兩面受壓的情況下才求和。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run as follows. Timing: under Emperor Wen in the last years of the Kaihuang reign the Khitan were already raiding Goryeo, and the Sui had campaigned there without finishing the matter; in the fourth month of the first year of Daye the emperor ordered the army out, and it was defeated; in the second year of Daye troops were sent again, the Khitan asked to surrender and were admitted, and the Sui set up commanderies for them; when the Sui collapsed the Khitan rebelled once more, and in the eighteenth year of Zhenguan they were admitted to the Tang. Strength: the histories record the Sui army as being proclaimed at three hundred thousand, which is the total of the expedition as given in the Comprehensive Mirror; the proportion that could actually be put into combat and into guarding the supply was far lower. The Khitan numbers are nowhere stated, only that they fought as mobile cavalry, their strength scattered among separate tribal camps, and the claim that their best horse numbered tens of thousands cannot be confirmed from any reliable record. Losses: in the first defeat the Sui army was broken, the dead were counted in tens of thousands, and the military stores and equipment were abandoned to the enemy; both the History of Sui and the Comprehensive Mirror compress this into a statement that very many were killed, with no finer figure. Distance: Liǔchéng commandery, in modern Liaoning at Cháoyáng, lies roughly one thousand five hundred li from the eastern capital Luoyáng, and several hundred li more separated it from the Songmo grassland of the Khitan, all grain moving in ox-drawn wagons over a round trip of more than two thousand li with no city in between in which to quarter it. Institutional figures: after the submission the Sui created commanderies and counties to settle them, the number settled is nowhere recorded, and it can only be inferred that it was part of the tribes rather than the whole people; in the second year of Daye the Sui still held the Qimin Qaghan as an ally in the north, squeezing the Khitan from that quarter, and it was under pressure from two directions that the Khitan sued for peace.
cause: 這場戰爭的起因是三層疊在一起的。第一層是直接的軍事藉口：契丹游騎越界寇掠高麗，高麗兵力不足以獨力抵禦，於是派使到隋廷請援，隋朝以救高麗的名義出兵，等於把自己的邊軍推上草原。第二層是隋文帝留下的舊賬：契丹在開皇末年已內侵高麗，隋廷出過兵，卻沒能羈縻住對方，戰後契丹復叛，這筆賬在煬帝手上變成了一筆必須償還的榮譽債，新君即位最需要的正是一場對外勝利。第三層是北方整體格局：契丹居於隋、突厥、高麗三面之間，草原上的部落要的是不被任何一方壓住，隋朝則要在他們南下的通道上插一面牆，於是先取契丹以制突厥成為大業初年北方的基本方針。推動此役的直接因素是高麗的請援與煬帝的北巡計畫：他在柳城一線巡行，軍糧、馬匹與行政樞紐都已就位，順手打一場草原戰爭在他看來成本低廉。真正的阻力卻來自草原本身，遠征所依賴的徵發丁壯、笨重車隊與中原式列陣，在沒有城牆可倚的開闊地帶毫無優勢，隋朝自己清楚這一點，只是把風險低估了。
causeEn: The causes of this war lie in three layers. The first is the immediate military pretext: Khitan outriders crossed the border and raided Goryeo, Goryeo's own troops were not enough to hold them off, so an embassy was sent to the Sui court asking for help, and the Sui marched out under the banner of relieving Goryeo, which amounted to pushing its own frontier army out onto the grassland. The second layer is an old score left by Emperor Wen: the Khitan had already raided Goryeo in the last years of Kaihuang, the Sui had sent troops and had not managed to hold them in submission, and after that campaign the Khitan rebelled again. In the hands of Emperor Yang that debt became a matter of prestige that had to be paid, and a new ruler needed above all a victory abroad. The third layer is the whole northern situation: the Khitan stood between the Sui, the Turks and Goryeo, the tribes of the steppe wanted to be pinned down by no one, and the Sui wanted to drive a stake into the corridor by which they moved south, so that taking the Khitan first in order to control the Turks became the settled northern policy of the early Daye years. What pushed the campaign into being was the plea from Goryeo and the emperor's plan for his northern tour: moving along the line of Liǔchéng, with grain, horses and the administrative machinery already in place, fighting a war on the grassland looked cheap. The real obstacle came from the grassland itself, for the levies, the heavy wagon train and the Chinese style of deploying on which a distant expedition depended were worthless in open country where there was no wall to lean on. The Sui knew this perfectly well and underestimated the risk all the same.
impact: 這場戰爭的第一重影響是打掉了隋煬帝即位時的銳氣。大業元年北方的敗仗，與同年林邑、南海方向的高調用兵同時出現在史書裡，讀史者常把它視作隋朝大興遠略而力不勝任的註腳：一名剛登基的皇帝在半年內同時向南海、東北兩個方向用兵，一勝一敗，而敗的那一次恰恰是硬碰硬的那一次。第二重影響在邊疆政策上：隋朝在東北方向改採以夷制夷，拉攏突厥的啟民可汗從北面壓住契丹，加上大業元年隋軍雖敗而未被全滅，契丹首領大業終於在大業二年遣使內附，隋廷於其地置州縣，把松漠的一部分部眾納入羈縻體系；內附的部眾在隋末亂局中相當一部分北走，剩下的則融入北方民族。往更長的時間看，這條線一直通向唐初：契丹在隋末復叛，又在唐貞觀年間內附，最終成為唐代東北的一支重要力量，經數百年分合之後建立遼朝。第三重影響在戰術與編制層面：這是中原王朝第一次以大規模常備兵正面撞上草原遊騎兵而敗北，隋軍靠徵發丁壯、層層設柵、糧道隨軍的作戰體系被證明不適合跨越數百里的草原，漢地與草原從此都記住了對方的長處。對隋朝自身，這場敗仗消耗的不只是兵員，還有剛剛建立起來的北伐信心，為大業年間連年用兵、最終引發民變埋下遠因。
impactEn: The first effect of this war was to take the edge off the new reign of Emperor Yang. The defeat in the north in the first year of Daye appears in the histories alongside the conspicuous campaigns of the same year against Lâm Ấp and the southern sea, and readers have long taken it as a footnote on the Sui's habit of reaching far beyond its strength: a ruler barely a year on the throne waging war at once to the south sea and to the north-east, one of them won and one lost, and the one that was lost was the one against a serious enemy. The second effect fell on frontier policy. In the north-east the Sui turned to using one barbarian against another, drawing the Qimin Qaghan of the Turks in to squeeze the Khitan from the north, and since the Sui army had been defeated but not destroyed in the first year of Daye, the Khitan chieftain Dà Yè finally sent an embassy to submit in the second year, and the court set up commanderies for part of the Songmo people, drawing them into a system of nominal allegiance. When the Sui fell, a good part of those settled people moved north again and the rest were absorbed into the northern peoples. Over the longer run the thread leads straight into the early Tang: the Khitan rebelled once more at the end of the Sui, were admitted again under the Zhenguan reign, and became an important power in the north-east of the Tang, eventually founding the Liao after centuries of division and union. The third effect lies in tactics and organisation. This was the first time a Chinese dynasty took a mass field army face to face against nomadic horse archers and lost, and the Sui system of levied infantry, layered stockades and a supply line tied to the marching column was proved unfit for crossing several hundred li of grassland; from that point both the Chinese plains and the steppe took note of what the other side could do. For the Sui itself the cost of this defeat was not only men but the confidence in northern campaigning that had just been built, and it lay far back among the causes of the endless wars of the Daye years and the revolt that finally broke the dynasty.

resultEn: The campaign at Liǔchéng in the fourth month of the first year of Daye ended in a great defeat for the Sui. An army proclaimed at three hundred thousand, having pushed deep into the grassland, was ground down by Khitan outriders; the baggage was raided, the column was cut, stores and equipment were lost, the dead were counted in tens of thousands, and an expedition of hundreds of thousands bought nothing but a collapse. In the second year of Daye the court sent troops again, the Khitan chieftain Dà Yè avoided battle and asked to surrender, the Sui set up commanderies for them, and Songmo was formally drawn into a system of allegiance. But this was not a conquest: the Khitan rebelled again at the end of the Sui, were admitted once more under the Zhenguan reign, and went on to the Liao much later. Back to the weapon on the card. The Assyrian bow was not at Liǔchéng; the chariot archers of Assyria had been used up long before the walls of Nineveh, and the Khitan horsemen of thirteen hundred years later held composite horn bows of the same structure and followed the same technical tradition in which the bowman sets the tempo of the fight. An Assyrian mixture of arrow rain and chariot charge has no answer on open grassland, while the steppe mixture of mobile horse and severed supply cut the Chinese infantry army to pieces. The campaign is therefore a report on archers written in defeat: what decided the fate of the Sui army was not the form of the bow but who controlled the moment of striking. The Sui lost because it had to fight on another people's pasture and at another people's tempo; the Khitan lost because they had no means to turn a single victory into permanent submission.
